Condition conventions

Source: R/conditions.R
anndata-conditions.Rd

Developer notes for raising errors and warnings inside the package.

Arguments

message

Message in cli style, interpolated in .envir.

class

Specific subclass, added after the generic one is prepended.

...

Further fields stored in the condition.

call

The call reported by the condition, by default the function that called the wrapper.

.envir

Environment used to interpolate message.

Details

All conditions go through cli::cli_abort() and cli::cli_warn() via the internal wrappers anndata_abort() and anndata_warn(). Every condition has class anndata_error or anndata_warning, a specific subclass named for the situation, and the rlang_error or rlang_warning class added by cli. Tests check classes rather than message text.

Python's categories map to these classes:

PythonR class
ImplicitModificationWarninganndata_implicit_modification_warning
FutureWarninganndata_future_warning
IORegistryErroranndata_io_registry_error
shape mismatchanndata_dimension_error
feature in a later sub-projectanndata_not_supported_error
values do not fit an On-disk dtypeanndata_dtype_overflow_error
dataset is not an integer or floatanndata_dtype_error

A Python logger.warning call becomes an anndata_warning subclass named for the situation too, and logger.info is signalled as the (silent unless handled) condition anndata_info_message. A Python UserWarning becomes an anndata_warning subclass named for the situation (e.g. anndata_names_not_unique_warning), and any other Python error becomes an anndata_error subclass named likewise. Use the named constructors (abort_dimension(), abort_io_registry(), abort_not_supported(), warn_implicit_modification(), warn_future()) for the classes above and anndata_abort() or anndata_warn() for new ones.
